1.note: Ezekiel is using the phrase translated as **And it was** to introduce a new event in the story. Use a word, phrase, or other method in your language that is natural for introducing a new event.

Here, **to my face** represents being in front of Ezekiel. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [and they sat before me]

2.note: Ezekiel is using **the word of Yahweh was to me** as a common expression of the culture to mean “Yahweh spoke a message to me.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [Then Yahweh spoke a message to me]
The term **saying** introduces a direct quotation. In your translation, use a natural way of introducing direct quotations in your language. It may not be necessary to represent this term explicitly.

3.note: See how you translated **Son of man** in [2:1](ta:02). This also occurs in verses 4, 27, and 46.

3.q: דַּבֵּ֞ר אֶת זִקְנֵ֤י יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ וְ⁠אָמַרְתָּ֣ אֲלֵ⁠הֶ֔ם כֹּ֤ה אָמַר֙ אֲדֹנָ֣⁠י יְהוִ֔ה
3.note: If it would be clearer in your language, you could translate this so that there is not a quotation within a quotation. Alternate translation: [speak to the elders of Israel and give them this message from the Lord Yahweh]

Ezekiel is using a future statement to give an instruction or command. If it would be helpful in your language, you could translate these words using a command or instruction form. Alternate translation: [and say to them]
See how you translated the similar expression in 2:4. This also occurs in verses 39 and 47.

Yahweh is using the question form to rebuke the elders and to show that he will not let them ask him for guidance. If a speaker of your language would not use the question form for that purpose, you could translate this as a statement or as an exclamation. Alternate translation: [You have no right to come and ask me what you should do!]

Following the custom of the culture, Yahweh is swearing an oath by stating the first part of a condition (“if”) but not the second part (“then”). The expression translated as **The life of me** means “As surely as I live.” Yahweh means that he will certainly not let the elders ask him for guidance. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could explicitly state the second part of this condition. Alternate translation: [As surely as I live, I will certainly not let you ask me for guidance]

The expression **I will be asked by you** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in an active form or in another way that is natural in your language. This also occurs in verse 31. Alternate translation: [I will let you inquire of me]
See how you translated **the declaration of the Lord Yahweh** in 5:11. This also occurs in verses 31, 33, 36, 40, and 44.

4.note: Yahweh is using the question form to command Ezekiel to judge the elders. If a speaker of your language would not use the question form for that purpose, you could translate this as a statement or as an exclamation. Alternate translation: [Judge them! Judge, son of man!]

The pronoun **them** refers to the elders of Israel who had come to Ezekiel. Some interpreters think it refers to the ancestors of the elders, whose sinful deeds Yahweh describes next. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [Will you judge these elders…Make those elders know]

Yahweh is using the term **fathers** to mean “ancestors.” If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. This also occurs in verses 18, 24, 27, 30, 36, and 42. Alternate translation: [the abominations of their ancestors]

5.note: Ezekiel is using a future statement to give an instruction or command. If it would be helpful in your language, you could translate the words **And you shall say to them** using a command or instruction form. Alternate translation: [And tell them]

Yahweh is using **On the day** as a common expression in the culture to mean “At the time when.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [At the time when I chose Israel]

Lifting the hand was a symbolic action by which a person showed that he was swearing an oath. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could explain the significance of this action in the text of your translation or in a footnote. This also occurs in verses 6, 15, 23, 28, and 42. This also occurs in verses 6 and 15. Alternate translation: [and I raised my hand as a sign that I was making a solemn promise… And I made a promise to them]

Here Yahweh is speaking as if the descendants of Jacob were **seed** that came from his **house**, that is, from his family. It means that they were the people who descended from Jacob. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [to the people who descended from Jacob]

5.q: וָ⁠אֶשָּׂ֨א יָדִ֤⁠י לָ⁠הֶם֙ לֵ⁠אמֹ֔ר אֲנִ֖י יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֵי⁠כֶֽם
5.note: If it would be clearer in your language, you could translate this so that there is not a quotation within a quotation. Alternate translation: [And I lifted my hand to them, and said that I am Yahweh, their God]

6.note: See how you translated the similar expression in 20:5.
See how you translated the similar expressions in 20:5.

Here Yahweh is speaking as if the land were **flowing with milk and honey**. It means that the land was very fertile and produced abundant food that was amply sufficient for their needs. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. This also occurs in verse 15. Alternate translation: [that could amply supply all of their food]

The pronoun **it** refers to the land that Yahweh had searched out for the Israelites, not to the milk and honey. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. This also occurs in verse 15. Alternate translation: [that land was beauty to all the lands]

Here, Yahweh is speaking as if the land were **beauty** itself. It means that the land was the most beautiful of all the lands. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [it was more beautiful than any other land]

7.note: Yahweh is not referring to a specific **man**. He means each of the Israelites in general. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could use an expression that would be more natural in your language. Alternate translation: [Each one of you, the detestations of your eye, throw away]

Here, **his eye** represents “what he desires.” If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [the detestations that he desires]
If your language does not use a noun for the idea of **detestations**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [the detestable things]

8.note: Ezekiel uses the word **But** here to indicate a contrast between what Yahweh commanded the Israelites in Egypt and how they responded. In your translation, indicate this contrast in a way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [However, they rebelled]

The implication is that the Israelites were not willing to obey what Yahweh told them, not merely that they would not hear him. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [and they were not willing to listen to what I told them to do and do it]

Ezekiel is not referring to a specific **man**. He means people in general. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could use an expression that would be more natural in your language. Alternate translation: [None one of them threw away the detestations of his eyes]
See how you handled this expression in 20:7.

Here Yahweh is speaking as if his **heat**, that is, his anger, were a liquid that he could **pour** on the Israelites. It means that he intended to punish them severely because he was very angry with them. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. This also occurs in verses 13 and 21. Alternate translation: [to punish them severely because of my anger]

Yahweh is the words **my heat** and **my nose** as common expressions in the culture to mean “my anger.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [my intense anger… my rage] or [my angry feelings… how angry I felt]

Yahweh is using **I said** as a common expression in the culture to mean “I decided.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. This also occurs in verses 13 and 21. Alternate translation: [So I decided to pour]
The word translated as **So** indicates that what follows is a result of what came before. Use a connector in your language that makes this clear. Alternate translation: [This is why I said]

Yahweh is using **to complete my nose against them** as a common expression in the culture to mean “to fully express my anger against them.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. This also occurs in verse 21. Alternate translation: [to fully unleash my anger against them]

9.note: God uses the word **But** here to indicate a contrast between what the Israelites deserved for their rebellion and what he actually did. In your translation, indicate this contrast in a way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [Nevertheless, I acted]

Here, **my name** represents “my reputation.” If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. This also occurs in verses 14, 22, and 44. Alternate translation: [for the sake of my reputation]

The expression **without being profaned** is a passive verbal form. It refers to the nations treating the name of Yahweh as if it were not holy. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [so that the nations would not consider it unholy]
See how you translated this expression in 5:8. This also occurs in verses 14, 22, and 41.

10.note: The pronoun **them** refers to the Israelites, the descendants of Jacob who were in Egypt. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [So I brought the descendants of Jacob out]

11.q: אֲשֶׁ֨ר יַעֲשֶׂ֥ה אוֹתָ֛⁠ם הָ⁠אָדָ֖ם וָ⁠חַ֥י בָּ⁠הֶֽם
11.note: Yahweh is presenting a possible condition, that a person will live if he obeys the statutes and judgments of Yahweh. Use a natural form in your language for introducing a condition that could happen. This also occurs in verses 13 and 21. Alternate translation: [If a person obeys them, then he will live by them]

Here, the masculine term **man** has a generic sense that includes both men and women. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could use language in your translation that is clearly inclusive of both men and women. Alternate translation: [Any man or woman who does them] or [Any person who does them]

12.note: It might seem that the expression **between me and between them** contains extra information that would not be natural to express in your language. If so, you could shorten it. Alternate translation: [between me and them]

Here, the words **to know** marks **that I am Yahweh, the one sanctifying them** as the goal or purpose of Yahweh giving the people **a sign**. Use a connector in your language that makes it clear that this is the purpose. Alternate translation: [so that they would know]
See how you translated the similar expression in 6:7. This also occurs in verses 20, 38, 42, and 44.

Yahweh is not distinguishing himself from another Yahweh who is not **sanctifying them**. Yahweh is reminding the Israelites that he is the one who sets them apart for himself. Be sure that this is clear in your translation. Alternate translation: [Yahweh, and that I sanctify them]

13.note: Ezekiel uses the word **But** here to indicate a contrast between what Yahweh did for the Israelites in the wilderness and how they responded to him. In your translation, indicate this contrast in a way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [However, the house of Israel rebelled]
See how you translated the similar expression in [3:1](ta:03). This also occurs in verses 27, 30, 31, 39, 40, and 44.

Here Yahweh is speaking as if his **statutes** were a path in which the Israelites could **walk**. It means that they did not live in the way that his statutes required. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. This also occurs in verses 16, 18, 19, and 21. Alternate translation: [They did not obey my statutes]
See how you translated the similar expression in 20:11.

13.q: וָ⁠אֹמַ֞ר לִ⁠שְׁפֹּ֨ךְ חֲמָתִ֧⁠י עֲלֵי⁠הֶ֛ם בַּ⁠מִּדְבָּ֖ר לְ⁠כַלּוֹתָֽ⁠ם
13.note: See how you handled the similar expression in 20:8.

14.note: Ezekiel uses the word **But** here to indicate a contrast between what the Israelites deserved for rebelling in the wilderness and what Yahweh did instead. In your translation, indicate this contrast in a way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [Nevertheless, I acted]

14.q: לְמַ֣עַן שְׁמִ֑⁠י לְ⁠בִלְתִּ֤י הֵחֵל֙ לְ⁠עֵינֵ֣י הַ⁠גּוֹיִ֔ם
14.note: See how you translated the similar expression in 20:9.

The pronouns **who** and **their** refer to the nations, and the pronoun **them** refers to the Israelites. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [before whose eyes I brought the Israelites out]

15.note: Yahweh is stating the pronoun **I** separately, even though the verb translated as **lifted** already includes this meaning. He is doing that to emphasize that he himself swore this oath. If a speaker of your language would use an explicit pronoun for the same purpose, you may want to use that construction in your translation. If not, your language may have other ways of showing the meaning here. This also occurs in verses 23 and 25. Alternate translation: [And I myself also lifted]
See how you translated the similar expression in 20:5

The implication is that Yahweh swore that he would not bring that generation of Israelites into the land. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [that I would not bring that generation of Israelites into the land]

The implication is that Yahweh had promised to give this land to the Israelites. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [that I had promised to give them]

15.q: זָבַ֤ת חָלָב֙ וּ⁠דְבַ֔שׁ צְבִ֥י הִ֖יא לְ⁠כָל־הָ⁠אֲרָצֽוֹת
15.note: See how you translated the similar expression in 20:6

16.note: The word translated as **because** indicates that what follows is a reason for what came before. Use a connector in your language that makes it clear that what follows is a reason for what came before. Alternate translation: [I did this because my judgments they rejected]

The word translated as **for** indicates that what follows is a reason for what came before. Use a connector in your language that makes it clear that what follows is a reason for what came before. Alternate translation: [They did this because after their idols, their heart was walking]

Here Yahweh is speaking as if the **heart** of the Israelites were a person **walking** behind their idols. It means that they eagerly desired to worship their idols. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [for they strongly wanted to worship their idols]

17.note: Ezekiel uses the word **But** here to indicate a contrast between the house of Israel’s rebellion and Yahweh’s pity on them. In your translation, indicate this contrast in a way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [Nevertheless, my eye had pity]

Yahweh is using **my eye** to represent himself. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression from your culture or state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [But I had pity on them]

Yahweh is using **make them a complete end** as a common expression of the culture to mean “destroy them completely.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and I did not wipe them out]

18.note: Here the masculine term **sons** has a generic sense that includes both men and women. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could use language in your translation that is clearly inclusive of both men and women. Alternate translation: [their sons and daughters]

Here, **your fathers** represents the previous generation of Israelites, including their ancestors in general. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [your ancestors]

20.note: The implication is that the Israelites were to keep the Sabbath days holy by setting them apart for Yahweh and by not working on them. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [And set apart my Sabbaths for me by not working on them]

Here, **to know** marks “that I am Yahweh your God” as the goal or purpose of the Sabbaths being “a sign between me and between you.” Use a connector in your language that makes it clear that this is the purpose.

21.note: Ezekiel uses the word **But** here to indicate a contrast between the sons and their fathers, who had also rebelled against Yahweh. In your translation, indicate this contrast in a way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [Yet the sons rebelled]

Here the masculine term **the sons** has a generic sense that includes both men and women. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could use language in your translation that is clearly inclusive of both men and women. Alternate translation: [the sons and daughters]
Yahweh speaks of a person obeying his statutes as if the **statutes** were a path along which the person walks. Alternate translation: [They did not obey my statutes]

21.q: אֲשֶׁר֩ יַעֲשֶׂ֨ה אוֹתָ֤⁠ם הָֽ⁠אָדָם֙ וָ⁠חַ֣י בָּ⁠הֶ֔ם
21.note: See how you translated the similar expression in 20:11.

21.q: וָ⁠אֹמַ֞ר לִ⁠שְׁפֹּ֧ךְ חֲמָתִ֣⁠י עֲלֵי⁠הֶ֗ם לְ⁠כַלּ֥וֹת אַפִּ֛⁠י בָּ֖⁠ם בַּ⁠מִּדְבָּֽר
21.note: See how you translated the similar expression in 20:08.

Yahweh speaks of expressing his fury by punishing them as if his fury were a liquid that he poured out on them. See how you translated this in 20:8. Alternate translation: [to act against them in my fury]

22.note: Yahweh is using **I returned my hand** as a common expression of the culture to mean “I held back from punishing them.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [But I refrained from punishing them]

22.q: וָ⁠אַ֖עַשׂ לְמַ֣עַן שְׁמִ֑⁠י לְ⁠בִלְתִּ֤י הֵחֵל֙ לְ⁠עֵינֵ֣י הַ⁠גּוֹיִ֔ם
22.note: See how you translated the similar expression in 20:9.
See how you translated the similar expression in 20:14.

23.note: See how you handled the similar expression in 20:15.
See how you handled the similar expression in 20:6.

23.q: לְ⁠הָפִ֤יץ אֹתָ⁠ם֙ בַּ⁠גּוֹיִ֔ם וּ⁠לְ⁠זָר֥וֹת אוֹתָ֖⁠ם בָּ⁠אֲרָצֽוֹת
23.note: The phrases **to scatter them among the nations** and **to disperse them among the lands** mean similar things. Yahweh is using the two phrases together for emphasis. If it would be clearer for your readers, you could express the emphasis with a single phrase. Alternate translation: [to scatter them far and wide among all the nations]

24.note: Yahweh is using **after the idols of their fathers, their eyes were** as a common expression of the culture to mean “they longed to worship the idols that their ancestors had worshiped.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and they longed to worship the idols that their fathers had worshiped]

25.note: See how you handled the similar expression in 20:15.

25.q: חֻקִּ֖ים לֹ֣א טוֹבִ֑ים וּ⁠מִ֨שְׁפָּטִ֔ים לֹ֥א & יִֽחְי֖וּ בָּ⁠הֶֽם
25.note: The terms **statutes not good** and **judgments that they could not live by them** mean similar things. Ezekiel is using the two terms together for emphasis. If it would be clearer for your readers, you could express the emphasis with a single phrase. Alternate translation: [harmful laws by which they could not truly live]

The implication is that Yahweh allowed the Israelites to follow harmful practices as a punishment for rejecting his good statutes. Some interpreters think Yahweh means that he let them follow the laws and customs of the nations. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [statutes that were not good for them, as a punishment]

26.note: Yahweh is referring to sacrificing children by burning them alive in a polite way, using the phrase **making every firstborn of the womb to pass**. Depending on what is helpful for your readers, you could use a polite way of referring to this in your language, or you could state this plainly. Alternate translation: [in making every firstborn of the womb to pass through the fire as a sacrifice]

Ezekiel is using this possessive form to mean the firstborn children who open the womb, that is, the first child born to each mother. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [every firstborn child]

The first **so that** marks “I might desolate them” as the goal or purpose of “I made them unclean by their gifts”. The second **so that** marks what follows as the goal or purpose of Yahweh making them desolate. Use a connector in your language that makes it clear that this is the purpose.

27.note: The term translated as **Therefore** indicates that what follows is a result of what came before. Use a connector in your language that makes this clear. Alternate translation: [Because of all this]

27.q: דַּבֵּ֨ר אֶל־בֵּ֤ית יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ & וְ⁠אָמַרְתָּ֣ אֲלֵי⁠הֶ֔ם כֹּ֥ה אָמַ֖ר אֲדֹנָ֣⁠י יְהוִ֑ה
27.note: If it would be clearer in your language, you could translate this so that there is not a quotation within a quotation. Alternate translation: [tell the house of Israel…that this is what the Lord Yahweh says to them]

The pronoun **this** refers to the sinful acts that Yahweh describes in the next verse. Some interpreters think it refers back to the rebellions in the wilderness that Yahweh has just described. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [Still by what I will now describe, your fathers blasphemed me]
If your language does not use a noun for the idea of **violation**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [when they were very unfaithful to me]

Ezekiel is using a construction in which a verb and its object come from the same root. You may be able to use the same construction in your language to express the meaning here. Alternatively, your language may have another way of saying this. Alternate translation: [when they were utterly unfaithful to me]

28.note: See how you handled the similar expression in 20:6.

28.q: כָל גִּבְעָ֨ה רָמָ֜ה וְ⁠כָל עֵ֣ץ עָבֹ֗ת
28.note: The implication is that the Israelites worshiped idols on **every high hill** and under **every leafy tree**, because people thought that those were good places to worship false gods. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [every high hill and every leafy tree, places where people worshiped false gods]

Ezekiel is using a construction in which a verb and its object come from the same root. You may be able to use the same construction in your language to express the meaning here. Alternatively, your language may have another way of saying this. Alternate translation: [and they offered their offerings there]

Here, **the anger of their offering** represents “their offering that made me angry.” If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [their offering that provoked me]
See how you translated the similar expression in 6:13. This also occurs in verse 41.

29.q: וָ⁠אֹמַ֣ר אֲלֵ⁠הֶ֔ם מָ֣ה הַ⁠בָּמָ֔ה אֲשֶׁר־אַתֶּ֥ם הַ⁠בָּאִ֖ים שָׁ֑ם
29.note: If it would be clearer in your language, you could translate this so that there is not a quotation within a quotation. Alternate translation: [And I asked them what the high place was to which they were going]

29.q: מָ֣ה הַ⁠בָּמָ֔ה אֲשֶׁר אַתֶּ֥ם הַ⁠בָּאִ֖ים שָׁ֑ם
29.note: Yahweh is using the question form to rebuke the Israelites for worshiping at the high place. If a speaker of your language would not use the question form for that purpose, you could translate this as a statement or as an exclamation. Alternate translation: [You should not be going to this high place to worship!]

29.q: וַ⁠יִּקָּרֵ֤א שְׁמָ⁠הּ֙ בָּמָ֔ה עַ֖ד הַ⁠יּ֥וֹם הַ⁠זֶּֽה
29.note: Yahweh is providing background information to help readers understand why that place was called **Bamah**. In your translation, introduce this information in a way that would be natural in your own language and culture.

The expression **its name was called** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [And people have called it Bamah]
The word **Bamah** is the name of a place. It is the same word that is translated as **the high place** earlier in this verse. You could include its meaning in your translation or in a footnote.

30.q: לָ⁠כֵ֞ן אֱמֹ֣ר אֶל־בֵּ֣ית יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל כֹּ֤ה אָמַר֙ אֲדֹנָ֣⁠י יְהוִ֔ה
30.note: If it would be clearer in your language, you could translate this so that there is not a quotation within a quotation. Alternate translation: [Therefore, tell the house of Israel that the Lord Yahweh says this]
The term translated as **Therefore** indicates that what follows is a result of what came before. Use a connector in your language that makes this clear. Alternate translation: [For this reason]

30.q: הַ⁠בְּ⁠דֶ֥רֶךְ אֲבֽוֹתֵי⁠כֶ֖ם אַתֶּ֣ם נִטְמְאִ֑ים וְ⁠אַחֲרֵ֥י שִׁקּוּצֵי⁠הֶ֖ם אַתֶּ֥ם זֹנִֽים
30.note: Yahweh is using the question form to accuse the Israelites of doing the same evil things that their ancestors did. If a speaker of your language would not use the question form for that purpose, you could translate this as a statement or as an exclamation. Alternate translation: [You are making yourselves unclean in the way of your fathers, and you are prostituting yourselves after their detestations!]

Here Yahweh is speaking as if the conduct of the ancestors of the Israelites were a **way**, that is, a path. It means that the Israelites were behaving in the same way as their ancestors. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [By acting just as your fathers did]
Here, **your fathers** represents “your ancestors.” If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [your forefathers]
If your language does not use a noun for the idea of **detestations**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [the detestable things they did]

Here Yahweh is speaking as if worshiping idols were **prostituting yourselves**. It means that by worshiping other gods, the Israelites were being unfaithful to Yahweh, just as a prostitute is sexually unfaithful. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [are you behaving disloyally toward me]

31.note: Ezekiel is using **when you lifted your gifts** as a common expression of the culture to mean “when you offered your sacrifices to the gods.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [And when you presented your gifts] or [And when you offered your sacrifices]
See how you handled the similar expression in 20:26.

Yahweh is using the question form to emphasize that he will not let the Israelites seek him for guidance. If a speaker of your language would not use the question form for that purpose, you could translate this as a statement or as an exclamation. Alternate translation: [And I will certainly not be sought by you, house of Israel!]

Here, **house of Israel** represents the people who are descendants of Israel. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [people of Israel]

31.q: חַי אָ֗נִי נְאֻם֙ אֲדֹנָ֣⁠י יְהוִ֔ה אִם אִדָּרֵ֖שׁ לָ⁠כֶֽם
31.note: Following the custom of the culture, Yahweh is swearing an oath by stating the first part of a condition (“if”) but not the second part (“then”). Yahweh means that he will certainly not let the Israelites seek him for guidance. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could explicitly state the second part of this condition. Alternate translation: [As surely as I live”—the declaration of the Lord Yahweh—“I will certainly not let you seek me for guidance]

32.note: Yahweh is using **the thing ascending on your spirit** as a common expression of the culture to mean “the thoughts coming into your mind.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [And the thing that comes into your mind]

Ezekiel is repeating forms of the verb **being** in order to intensify his expression of the idea that it conveys. If your language can repeat words for intensification, it would be appropriate to do that here in your translation. If not, your language may have another way of expressing the intensification. Alternate translation: [it will certainly not happen]

If it would be clearer in your language, you could translate this so that there is not a quotation within a quotation. Alternate translation: [that you are saying that you want to become like the nations]

Here, **wood and stone** represent “idols made from wood and stone.” If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [to serve idols made from wood and stone]

33.q: חַי אָ֕נִי נְאֻ֖ם אֲדֹנָ֣⁠י יְהוִ֑ה אִם לֹ֠א
33.note: Following the custom of the culture, Yahweh is swearing an oath by stating the first part of a condition (“if”) but not the second part (“then”). By saying **if not**, Yahweh means that he will certainly do what he says next. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could explicitly state the second part of this condition. Alternate translation: [As surely as I live”—the declaration of the Lord Yahweh—“it is certain that]

The terms **with a strong hand** and **with an outstretched arm** mean similar things. Both refer to the great power of Yahweh. Yahweh is using the two terms together for emphasis. If it would be clearer for your readers, you could express the emphasis with a single phrase. This also occurs in verse 34. Alternate translation: [with very great power]

The expression **heat poured out** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. This also occurs in verse 34. Alternate translation: [and with heat that I pour out]

Yahweh is using the phrase **and with heat poured out** as a common expression of the culture to mean “and with a great expression of anger.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and with burning rage] or [and with intense anger]

34.note: The expression **you were scattered** is a passive verbal form. Yahweh is the one who scattered them. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [in which I scattered you]

34.q: בְּ⁠יָ֤ד חֲזָקָה֙ וּ⁠בִ⁠זְר֣וֹעַ נְטוּיָ֔ה וּ⁠בְ⁠חֵמָ֖ה שְׁפוּכָֽה
34.note: See how you translated the similar expressions in 20:33.

35.note: The implication is that **the wilderness of the peoples** is a desert region among the nations where Yahweh would judge the Israelites, just as he judged their ancestors in the wilderness after they left Egypt. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [the desert region among the nations, a wilderness like the one where I judged your ancestors]

Yahweh is using **face to face** as a common expression of the culture to mean “directly and personally.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [directly and personally]

37.note: Here, Yahweh is speaking as if he were a shepherd and the Israelites were sheep that he would make **pass under the rod**. A shepherd would hold his rod over his sheep as they passed by in order to count and examine them. It means that Yahweh would carefully examine each of the Israelites. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [And I will carefully examine each one of you]

Here, Yahweh is speaking as if the covenant were a **bond** that tied the Israelites to him. It means that Yahweh would make the Israelites keep his covenant. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [under the obligation of the covenant]

Ezekiel is using the possessive form to describe a **bond** that is characterized by **the covenant**. If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. Alternate translation: [into the binding obligation of the covenant]

38.note: Here, Yahweh is speaking as if the rebels were impurities that he would **purge** from metal. It means that he would remove the rebels from among the Israelites. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [And I will remove from among you the rebels]
If your language does not use a noun for the idea of **sojournings**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [From the land where they have been staying temporarily]

Ezekiel is using the possessive form to describe a land where the people have been living as foreigners. The expression **the land of their sojournings** means “the land in which they have lived as foreigners.” If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. Alternate translation: [From the land where they have lived as foreigners]

In this verse, the word **he** is singular in form, but it refers to all the rebels as a group. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use the plural form of “he.” Alternate translation: [but to the land of Israel, they will not come]

39.note: Yahweh actually means to communicate the opposite of the literal meaning of what he is saying here. He does not want the Israelites to serve their idols. If a speaker of your language would not do that, you could translate the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [Each man, go ahead and serve his idols, if you insist on doing that]

Here, the masculine term **A man** has a generic sense that includes both men and women. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could use language in your translation that is clearly inclusive of both men and women. Alternate translation: [Any man or woman, their idols]

Yahweh is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You can supply these words from the context if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [and afterward keep on serving them, if you are not going to listen to me]

Ezekiel is using **A man** as a common expression of the culture to mean “each person.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [Each of you] or [Everybody]

Yahweh is using the possessive form to describe a **name** that is characterized by **holiness**. If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. Alternate translation: [my holy name]

Here, **the name of my holiness** represents Yahweh himself, who is holy. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [me, Yahweh, who is holy]

40.note: The word translated as **For** indicates that what follows is a reason for what came before. Use a connector in your language that makes it clear that what follows is a reason for what came before. Alternate translation: [This is because]

The implication is that **the mountain of my holiness** is Mount Zion in Jerusalem, where the temple was. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [on Mount Zion in Jerusalem, the mountain of my holiness where my temple is, on the mountain of the height of Israel]

Ezekiel is using this possessive form to mean the mountain that is set apart for Yahweh, which is holy because it belongs to him. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [on my holy mountain]

Yahweh is using the possessive form to describe a **mountain** that is characterized by **height**. If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. Alternate translation: [on the high mountain of Israel]

41.note: Here, Yahweh is speaking as if the Israelites were a sacrifice with **an aroma of pleasing** that he would **accept**. It means that Yahweh would be pleased with the Israelites and accept them, just as he was pleased with sacrifices that people offered to him properly. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [With great pleasure, I will accept you]

Ezekiel is using the possessive form to describe an aroma that is characterized by being **pleasing**. If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. Alternate translation: [With a pleasing aroma]

The expression **I will be sanctified** is a passive verbal form. It means that the nations will see that Yahweh is holy. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [then I will show myself to be holy among you]

Here, **to the eyes of the nations** represents the nations seeing what Yahweh does. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [in the sight of the nations]

42.q: אֶל־אַדְמַ֣ת יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל אֶל־הָ⁠אָ֗רֶץ אֲשֶׁ֤ר נָשָׂ֨אתִי֙ אֶת־יָדִ֔⁠י לָ⁠תֵ֥ת אוֹתָ֖⁠הּ לַ⁠אֲבֽוֹתֵי⁠כֶֽם
42.note: The terms **to the land of Israel** and **to the land that I lifted my hand to give it to your fathers** mean similar things. Yahweh is using the two phrases together for emphasis. If it would be clearer for your readers, you could express the emphasis with a single phrase. Alternate translation: [to the land of Israel that I promised to give to your fathers]

Lifting the hand was a symbolic action by which Yahweh showed that he was solemnly swearing a promise. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could explain the significance of this action in the text of your translation or in a footnote. Alternate translation: [that I solemnly promised to give]
Here, **your fathers** represents “your ancestors.” If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [to your forefathers]

43.note: By **there**, Ezekiel means in the land of Israel, where God will bring the people back. You could indicate this explicitly in your translation if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [in that land of Israel]

Here Ezekiel is speaking of how a person lives as if that were a **way** or path that the person was walking along. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [how you lived]
Alternate translation: [with which you defiled yourselves]
See how you translated this expression in 6:9.
If your language does not use a noun for the idea of **evils**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [by all the evil things that you did]

44.note: Ezekiel is using the term **name** to represent who the person is or to refer to the person’s reputation. Alternate translation: [my reputation]

The phrases **your evil ways** and **your ruined deeds** mean similar things. Yahweh is using the two phrases together for emphasis. If it would be clearer for your readers, you could express the emphasis with a single phrase. Alternate translation: [not according to all the very wicked things that you have done]

Here Ezekiel is speaking of how a person lives as if that were a **way** or path that the person was walking along. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [according to your evil behavior]

46.note: Yahweh is using **set your face** as a common expression of the culture to mean “to turn one’s attention towards something in order to oppose it.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [focus your attention toward Teman in order to oppose it]

The terms **the way** and **Teman** mean similar things. Ezekiel is using the two terms together to mean “the way toward Teman.” If it would be clearer for your readers, you could express the emphasis with a single phrase. Alternate translation: [toward Teman]
The words **Teman** and **Darom** are names for the region to the south. Both words mean “south,” so you could also translate them as “the south.”

Here Yahweh is speaking as if the words of Ezekiel were a liquid that he could **drivel**, that is, cause to drip. It means that Ezekiel should speak his prophecy against the south. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and speak your prophecy against Darom]

Ezekiel is speaking to **the forest of the field of the Negev**, which he knows cannot hear him. He is doing this to communicate to the people listening to him that he feels very strongly about the coming judgment on the land. If it would be helpful in your language, you could translate these words as if he were speaking directly to the people about **the forest of the field of the Negev**. Alternate translation: [the people of the southern land]

The word **Negev** is a Hebrew word that refers to a southern desert region of the land of Israel. You will need to decide if you will use this word in its Hebrew form or if you will instead translate the meaning into your language. Either approach has broad support. If you use the Hebrew word, you could spell it the way it sounds in your language and then put the translation in a footnote. Alternate translation: [the southern region]

47.q: וְ⁠אָֽמַרְתָּ֙ לְ⁠יַ֣עַר הַ⁠נֶּ֔גֶב שְׁמַ֖ע דְּבַר יְהוָ֑ה כֹּֽה אָמַ֣ר אֲדֹנָ֣⁠י יְהוִ֡ה
47.note: If it would be clearer in your language, you could translate this so that there is not a quotation within a quotation. Alternate translation: [And you shall tell the forest of the Negev to hear the word of Yahweh, for this is what the Lord Yahweh says]

Yahweh is telling Ezekiel to speak to **the forest of the Negev**, which cannot hear him. If it would be helpful in your language, you could translate these words as if Ezekiel were speaking directly to the people of Judah. Alternate translation: [And you shall say to the people of Judah, whom the forest of the Negev represents]

Yahweh is using **Look at me** as a common expression of the culture to mean “I am about to.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [I am about to kindle]
The word **you** is singular here because Yahweh is addressing **the forest of the Negev**, so use the singular form in your translation if your language marks that distinction.

Here Yahweh is speaking as if his judgment were **a fire** that he would kindle in a forest. It means that he would destroy the people of Judah. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [bringing on you a judgment that is like a fire]

Yahweh is speaking of **a fire** as if it were a living thing that could **eat**. It means that the fire would burn up everything. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and it will burn up in you]

47.q: כָל עֵֽץ לַח֩ וְ⁠כָל עֵ֨ץ יָבֵ֤שׁ
47.note: Yahweh is referring to all of the trees in the forest by naming two major components: **every fresh tree** and **every dry tree**. Since the forest represents the people of Judah, this means all the people of Judah. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [every tree without exception]

The expression **will not be quenched** is a passive verbal form. It means that no one will be able to put out the fire. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [No one will be able to extinguish the flame of the blaze]
Ezekiel is using this possessive form to mean a flame that comes from a blazing fire. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [The flaming fire]

47.q: וְ⁠נִצְרְבוּ בָ֥⁠הּ כָּל פָּנִ֖ים מִ⁠נֶּ֥גֶב צָפֽוֹנָ⁠ה
47.note: The expression **will be scorched by it** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [and it will scorch all faces from the south to the north]

Yahweh is using **all faces** to represent every part of the forested land. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression from your culture or state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [all land]

Yahweh is referring to all of the land by naming two major components: **the south** and **the north**. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [in the whole land]

48.note: Yahweh is using **all flesh** to represent all people. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression from your culture or state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [And all people will see]

The pronoun **it** refers to the fire that Yahweh kindled. Some interpreters think it refers to the forest that the fire burned. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [I, Yahweh, have caused that fire to burn]

The expression **It will not be quenched** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. If you need to say who does the action, the context indicates that it is people. Alternate translation: [No one will put it out]

49.note: See how you translated this phrase in 4:14.

49.q: הֵ֚מָּה אֹמְרִ֣ים לִ֔⁠י הֲ⁠לֹ֛א מְמַשֵּׁ֥ל מְשָׁלִ֖ים הֽוּא
49.note: If it would be clearer in your language, you could translate this so that there is not a quotation within a quotation. Alternate translation: [They are saying about me that I am just a user of proverbs]

The people are using the question form to mock Ezekiel and to show that they did not take his message seriously. If a speaker of your language would not use the question form for that purpose, you could translate this as a statement or as an exclamation. Alternate translation: [He is just a user of proverbs!]

The pronoun **he** refers to Ezekiel himself. The people are speaking about Ezekiel. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [Is this Ezekiel not a user of proverbs]

Here, **a user of proverbs** is an emphatic construction that uses a verb and its object that come from the same root. You may be able to use the same construction in your language to express the meaning here. Alternatively, your language may have another way of showing the emphasis.
